pathogen_scientific_name.quote: The white pine blister rust fungus  Cronartium ribicola  needs to infect both white pine and a Ribes spp. plant to complete its life cycle.

type_of_disease.quote: Fungal Disease White Pine Blister Rust Cronartium ribicola

affected_parts.quote: White pine blister rust (WPBR) kills branches, tree tops and whole trees of Eastern white pine and causes leaf spots and leaf loss in currant and gooseberry plants.

summary.value: On Eastern white pine, needles on infected branches turn yellow then rusty red, and branches develop swollen cankers with discolored, cracked bark that ooze sticky sap and form white-to-yellow blisters releasing orange spores. On Ribes plants (currant and gooseberry), angular yellow leaf spots appear on the upper leaf surface with raised orange pustules on the underside.
summary.quote: All needles on one or more individual branches first turn yellow, then rusty red. The branch with the dead needles will have a canker which is a swollen area with discolored and cracked bark.

diagnostic_features.value: On pine: cankers on the main trunk are oval or diamond-shaped, often with a dead branch in the center, oozing sticky clear-to-white sap, with white-to-yellow blisters releasing powdery orange spores and gummy orange spore droplets. On Ribes: angular yellow leaf spots contained by leaf veins with raised orange pustules and orange or brown hair-like tendrils on the leaf underside.
diagnostic_features.quote: Cankers on the main trunk are oval or diamond-shaped and often have a dead branch in the center. Sticky, clear-to-white sap oozes from the canker and drips from the infected branch or runs down the trunk. In spring, white-to-yellow blisters form at the edge of the canker and release powdery orange spores.

value: Diseased pine branches should be pruned out of the tree before the infection comes within 4 inches of the main trunk.
Prune off branches with cankers at a branch union or where the branch meets the trunk. Remove at least 4 inches of healthy wood beyond the visible symptoms of disease.
Remove lower branches gradually as the trees mature; never remove more than 1/3 of the canopy at a time.
When planting white pine trees, space plants to promote good air movement around the trees. Redirect lawn sprinklers or irrigation systems to avoid wetting pine needles.
Don't plant eastern white pine and currants or gooseberry together in the landscape unless resistant cultivars are used. Avoid planting white pine in low lying areas or cold pockets.
Plant resistant varieties â€” 'Paton's Silver Splendor' eastern white pine and resistant gooseberry and currant cultivars are available.
Eradicating Ribes plants has not worked to eliminate the disease but may help slow the disease spread.

Pruning off the lower branches can help if done before rust symptoms on the branches get within six inches of the trunk; pruned branches can be left since the pathogen cannot survive in dried out tissue.
If symptoms develop within six inches of the trunk, removal of the tree is suggested to help reduce spread of disease.
treatments.quote: Diseased pine branches should be pruned out of the tree before the infection comes within 4 inches of the main trunk. Disease resistant currant and gooseberry bushes are available.

conflicts.note: UMN Extension explicitly states whole trees are killed (Whole plant); Illinois Extension lists only foliar (needles) and stem (cankers on branches/trunk) symptoms without a separate whole-plant designation.
